The name शरद carries the meaning “Autumn, Maturity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. data.cultural_impact: The name Sharad carries a rich cultural significance as it is associated with the harvest season in Hindu traditions. During this time, people come together to celebrate the abundance of their harvest and give thanks to the gods for their blessings. The name Sharad continues to be used as a popular given name in Hindu communities, especially in India and Nepal, and is seen as a symbol of the maturity and wisdom that comes with the autumn season.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sharad holds deep spiritual significance as it is the name of the divine goddess Sharada. She is revered as the goddess of knowledge, wisdom, and creativity. Sharada is believed to bestow her blessings upon those who seek knowledge and wisdom, helping them to gain a deeper understanding of the world and their place in it. She is also known to be the consort of Lord Shiva, making this name a powerful reminder of the union of Shiva and Shakti, the masculine and feminine energies, and the balance and harmony that exists in the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Sharda symbolizes the grace and beauty of Goddess Saraswati during the harvest season of Sharad Ritu (autumn). It embodies wisdom, creativity, and the nourishing blessings of nature.

historical_references.reference: Sharada was an incarnation of the goddess Saraswati, the goddess of learning and knowledge. She appeared during the Mahabharata war to bless Arjuna and help him win the battle.
historical_references.context: Mythology and religion, Mahabharata war era

historical_references.reference: The month of Sharad (October-November) was known as the season of harvest and was celebrated as Sharad Purnima, a major harvest festival in ancient India.
historical_references.context: Agriculture and festivals, ancient Indian society

modern_usage.modern_context: The Hindu month of शरद (Sharad) is celebrated as the season of harvest and romance. It is a time when people decorate their homes with autumn leaves and flowers, share pictures of their harvest on Instagram, plan their weddings on Pinterest and write poetry and stories about love on blogs.
